elements.label: Table D1
elements.details:
| Python Function | Description | Syntax | First Reference |
|-----------------|-------------|--------|-----------------|
| norm.cdf() | Calculates probabilities associated with the normal distribution (returns the area under the normal probability density function to the left of a specified measurement) | norm.cdf(x, mu, std)
Where:
x is the measurement of interest,
mu is the mean of the normal distribution,
std is the standard deviation of the normal distribution. | Discrete and Continuous Probability Distributions |
| t.ppf() | Generates the value of the t-distribution corresponding to a specified area under the t-distribution curve and specified degrees of freedom | t.ppf(area to left, degrees of freedom) | Statistical Inference and Confidence Intervals |
| bootstrap() | Performs bootstrap process to generate confidence interval | bootstrap(data, statistic, confidence_level, number_resamples) | Statistical Inference and Confidence Intervals |
elements.summary: This table summarizes Python functions useful for statistical analysis, including norm.cdf for normal distribution probabilities, t.ppf for t-distribution quantiles, and bootstrap for generating confidence intervals.
